3. Directed by John Huston and based on a screenplay by Arthur Miller (who wrote it as a "Valentine" for his then-wife Marilyn Monroe), the 1961 film The Misfits is historically regarded as the somber epitaph of the Golden Age of Hollywood.
The production was famously grueling, filmed in the 100°F heat of the Nevada desert. While the film provided a career-best dramatic turn for Marilyn Monroe, it also served as the final completed screen appearance for her legendary co-star. This "King of Hollywood," known for his rugged masculinity, suffered a fatal heart attack just days after filming wrapped—reportedly exacerbated by the physical strain of performing his own stunts with wild horses. Whose swansong was The Misfits?
